overview: This 343-page file chiefly compiles U.S. Embassy translations of Japanese commercial messages intercepted at Chungking from late 1943 through April 1944. They document wartime trade, shipping, shortages, prices, permits, finance, and industrial activity across East and Southeast Asia. Other records assess Hainan’s economic and strategic value, Japan’s domestic conditions, and proposals for its postwar economy.
interest: The intercepted business traffic offers unusually detailed evidence of everyday commerce and supply problems under Japanese occupation. The Hainan report and postwar policy critique add strategic and planning perspectives.
